title: Directories & registries
description: Where to discover more: MCP registries, awesome-lists, skill and plugin marketplaces.

items.name: ComposioHQ/awesome-claude-skills
items.description: Curated list of 1,000+ Claude skills and plugins across Claude.ai, Claude Code and other agents.
items.why: Good discovery source; vet individual skills before installing.

items.name: hesreallyhim/awesome-claude-code
items.description: Hand-picked collection of resources for Claude Code: skills, hooks, slash commands, plugins.
items.why: Best curated Claude Code resource index.

items.name: BehiSecc/awesome-claude-skills
items.description: Awesome-list of Claude skills (about 8.4k stars as of April 2026 per Star History).
items.why: Alternative skills list; smaller than Composio.

items.name: claudemarketplaces.com
items.description: Independent directory of Claude Code plugins, skills and MCP servers ranked by installs, stars and votes.
items.why: Handy browsing; not affiliated with Anthropic.

items.name: MCP Registry
items.description: Community-driven registry service for MCP servers; live at registry.modelcontextprotocol.io.
items.why: Canonical discovery source for MCP servers.

items.name: punkpeye/awesome-mcp-servers
items.description: Large categorized list of MCP servers, linked to glama.ai/mcp/servers.
items.why: Largest MCP index; use to find YouTube/video/image/social servers.

items.name: Glama MCP multimedia category
items.description: Glama directory category for multimedia MCP servers.

items.name: awesome-motion-design-agent-skills
items.description: A map of 5 first-party skills, 10 engine projects (GSAP, Motion, R3F, Remotion, Anime.js, Rive, dotLottie, Phaser) and 7 third-party packs, with link checks and advice to scan third-party packs before installing. Search also showed a larger catalogue, zhuyansen/awesome-claude-video-skills (about 180 repos, each security-graded): not opened.
items.verdictNote: REFERENCE: use as a directory; never install from a list without reading the skill.
items.why: 2 stars; counts are 'discovery signals, not rankings'
items.source: research 2026-10: content, motion, 3D and game tools

items.name: awesome-selfhosted
items.description: The main directory of free software you can run on your own server (about 1,400 linked projects): automation, analytics, media, CRM, docs, mail, monitoring and more, each with licence and language. Last commit 2026-10-22.
items.verdictNote: adopt: first stop before paying for a SaaS tool
items.why: Best source of self-hostable alternatives (n8n, Postiz-style schedulers, analytics) to keep monthly costs down. Being listed is not a review: check each project's activity, licence and security before running it on a server.

items.name: awesome-python
items.description: Curated list of Python frameworks, libraries and tools by category (about 560 links): web, data, scraping, CLI, testing, ML and more. Last commit 2026-10-23.
items.verdictNote: adopt: reference when Claude writes Python
items.why: Useful for picking a well-known library instead of an obscure one when automation scripts are built in Python. A directory, not a quality ranking.

items.name: The Book of Secret Knowledge
items.description: Large collection of command-line tools, one-liners, cheat sheets, blogs and security resources for sysadmins and DevOps.
items.why: Handy for server and network troubleshooting, but last commit 2024-11-19, so some links and tools are stale. Includes offensive-security tools: use those only on systems you own or are authorised to test.

items.name: awesome-go
items.description: Curated list of Go frameworks, libraries and software (about 3,000 links), with quality requirements for new entries. Last commit 2026-10-23.
items.verdictNote: reference: only if a project is written in Go
items.why: Well maintained, but current projects use Node.js and Python; useful mainly when choosing Go-based self-hosted tools.
